description: Settings reliability & consistency polish: shared accessible AlertDialog primitive, unified destructive confirmations, inline error surfacing + field-error a11y, dirty-form tab-switch guard, System tab accuracy, empty-state CTAs, label-catalog search, and typography baseline (web-only).

tasks.title: Add shared AlertDialog primitive; migrate Agent reset + IssueDetail comment delete
tasks.spec: specs/destructive-confirmation/spec.md#A shared accessible AlertDialog primitive is provided (+ #All destructive operations confirm through the shared AlertDialog: Agent reset, Issue comment delete)
tasks.description: Add packages/web/src/shared/ui/components/alert-dialog.tsx composing the existing dialog.tsx primitives (base-ui owns focus trap, focus restore, Escape, aria-modal). It is a controlled, role/affordance specialization: destructive-tone confirm button, no close X by default, opinionated two-button footer. Use it to replace the hand-written `fixed inset-0` reset modal in AgentSettingsSection and the `window.confirm` comment-delete in IssueDetailPage.tsx. Add a focused alert-dialog unit/a11y test and update the two section tests.
acceptanceCriteria: AlertDialog exists at shared/ui/components/alert-dialog.tsx and is built on dialog.tsx (no new dialog dependency, no hand-rolled focus trap).
Unit test asserts: focus moves into the dialog on open, Tab/Shift-Tab cycles within it, focus restores to the invoker on close, Escape cancels (no onConfirm fired).
Agent reset opens the shared AlertDialog; reset does NOT execute until confirm; the hand-written `fixed inset-0` reset modal is gone.
IssueDetailPage comment delete opens the shared AlertDialog; window.confirm is not invoked; comment is not deleted until confirm.
A repo-wide grep asserts no `window.confirm`/`window.alert` remains for destructive ops and no hand-written `fixed inset-0` confirm overlay remains.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` are green.
tasks.output: shared/ui/components/alert-dialog.tsx + alert-dialog.test.tsx; updated AgentSettingsSection.tsx (reset flow) and IssueDetailPage.tsx (comment delete) + their tests.
tasks.notes: Foundational primitive; every other destructive migration and the dirty-guard reuse it. Per design D1/D2/D9 (Slice A). Use controlled API mirroring NewTemplateDialog; per-call-site open state + pending target.

tasks.title: Route label/template/repository deletes through AlertDialog
tasks.spec: specs/destructive-confirmation/spec.md#All destructive operations confirm through the shared AlertDialog (Label-definition delete, Repository remove, Template delete scenarios)
tasks.description: In LabelCatalogSection, TemplatesSection, and RepositoriesSection, replace the current single-click immediate delete/remove with a per-section AlertDialog driven by a `pendingKey` state: the trigger button sets the pending target and opens the dialog; onConfirm runs the mutation against that target and closes on success. Reuse ONE AlertDialog instance per section (not one per row). Update each section's tests to assert confirmation-before-delete.
acceptanceCriteria: Label-definition delete, template delete, and repository remove each open the shared AlertDialog before executing.
The delete/remove mutation is NOT called on the initial trigger click; it runs only on confirm.
Each list section uses a single AlertDialog instance with a pending-target state (no per-row dialogs).
Section tests assert the dialog appears on trigger and the mutation is not invoked before confirm.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` are green.
tasks.output: Updated LabelCatalogSection.tsx, TemplatesSection.tsx, RepositoriesSection.tsx (delete/remove flows) + their tests.
tasks.notes: Per design D2/D9 (Slice B destructive portion). These sections currently have NO confirmation at all (single-click fire).

tasks.title: Surface Agent save/reset failures inline; extract FieldError helper and wire field-error a11y
tasks.spec: specs/settings-form-reliability/spec.md#Settings save and reset failures surface inline to the user (+ #Settings field errors are exposed to assistive technology)
tasks.description:
Replace the empty `catch {}` in AgentSettingsSection handleSave and confirmReset with `catch (err) { setSaveError(message(err)) }`; upgrade the existing saveError surface to a `role="alert"` red-700 card wrapped with `aria-live="polite"`. Extract a tiny shared FieldError helper (shared/ui/components/field-error.tsx: a `role="alert"`

with a stable useId, red-700 token) and use it for Agent InputField errors and Label-catalog add/edit field errors. Wire `aria-describedby={errorId}` + `aria-invalid={!!error}` on those inputs (mirror PreferencesSection). Add label-catalog + inbox to the a11y matrix.
acceptanceCriteria: handleSave failure sets saveError and renders inline role="alert" feedback; no empty catch block remains.
confirmReset failure sets saveError inline; no empty catch block remains.
Critical failure feedback is persistent-inline (role=alert + aria-live=polite); NO sonner/RuntimeToast call is added (not toast-only).
Agent InputField sets aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at its error element when an error is present.
Label-catalog create/edit fields set aria-invalid + aria-describedby on their inputs.
FieldError helper is extracted and used; error color converges on the red-700 token family (no text-red-600/text-red-700 drift).
label-catalog and inbox are added to tests/a11y/settings-a11y.test.tsx and the a11y run is green.
Tests assert inline error on save/reset failure and the aria wiring; typecheck + tests green.
tasks.output: shared/ui/components/field-error.tsx; updated AgentSettingsSection.tsx (catch + InputField a11y), LabelCatalogSection.tsx (field a11y); extended settings-a11y.test.tsx matrix + section tests.
tasks.notes: Per design D3/D4. FieldError is intentionally minimal — no app-wide <Field> wrapper refactor (out of scope). Keep styling on red-700/amber-700 tokens so the settings-consistency contract test stays green.

tasks.title: Guard unsaved Agent form changes on Settings tab switch
tasks.spec: specs/settings-form-reliability/spec.md#A dirty Settings form warns before tab switches discard unsaved changes
tasks.description: NOTE: App.tsx uses the legacy BrowserRouter (verified), so react-router useBlocker is a no-op — implement the design's documented fallback (design D5/Risks): intercept Settings sub-nav navigation. Add a settings-scoped SettingsDirtyContext provider in SettingsPage exposing setDirty(bool); AgentSettingsSection calls setDirty(dirty) in an effect (the `dirty` memo already exists). SettingsSubNav intercepts its tab <Link> onClick: when dirty, preventDefault and open the shared AlertDialog ('Discard unsaved changes?'); confirm proceeds with navigation, cancel keeps the form.
acceptanceCriteria: With a dirty Agent form, selecting another Settings sub-nav item opens the AlertDialog and does NOT silently discard unsaved changes.
With a clean Agent form, tab switches proceed with no prompt.
Confirm proceeds to the requested tab; cancel reverts and preserves the dirty form.
Guard is wired via a settings-scoped context (default not-dirty); a section that does not call setDirty is simply unguarded (graceful no-op).
Test asserts dirty -> prompt -> confirm proceeds, and clean -> no prompt.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` are green.
tasks.output: SettingsDirtyContext + provider in SettingsPage; SettingsSubNav onClick intercept; AgentSettingsSection setDirty wiring; AlertDialog 'discard changes' instance + tests.
tasks.notes: Spec scopes the guard to sub-nav-initiated switches, which the fallback satisfies fully. Reusing AlertDialog from T-001. Dialog copy must be generic ('Discard unsaved changes?').

tasks.title: Fix System tab metadata accuracy and relocate orphan edit-config banner
tasks.spec: specs/settings-content-consistency/spec.md#System settings metadata reflects real server-provided values (+ #System settings relocates the orphan edit-config banner)
tasks.description:
In SystemSettingsSection, replace the hardcoded `~/.mohist/logs/` Log Path (currently a mono

) with `systemInfo.paths.logs ?? '—'`, reading from the same useSystemInfo query the adjacent Paths card uses. Relocate the orphan amber 'Modify server-side config by editing config.jsonc...' banner into its related card as an inline amber note (preferred, matching existing in-card amber notes / WorkflowProfilesSection blocked-message pattern) or convert to an info Tooltip on that card's heading; normalize the amber shade to one token.
acceptanceCriteria: Log Path renders the value of systemInfo.paths.logs (falling back to '—'), NOT the hardcoded string; it matches the Paths card logs entry.
The edit-config guidance no longer renders as a standalone detached amber banner; it appears inside its related card or as an info tooltip.
Amber shade is normalized to a single token (no text-amber-700/text-amber-800 drift).
Tests assert Log Path equals systemInfo.paths.logs and the banner is not an orphan element.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` are green.
tasks.output: Updated SystemSettingsSection.tsx (Log Path source + banner relocation) + tests.
tasks.notes: Per design D8. Localized fixes only; no data model change.

tasks.title: Add next-step CTAs to Settings no-project and empty-list states
tasks.spec: specs/settings-content-consistency/spec.md#Settings empty states carry an explicit next-step action
tasks.description: Extend the existing SectionState (not a new EmptyState primitive) with an optional `action?: ReactNode` and a `no-project` variant (dashed box + select/create-project CTA). Replace the bare 'No project selected' markup in Repositories, Label catalog, Templates, and Workflows with this no-project variant. Give Label-catalog and Templates empty-list states an inline next-step CTA ('New definition' / 'New Template') via `action`, triggering the same create affordance already in each section header. Add a SectionState snapshot/contract to lock the additive API.
acceptanceCriteria: No-project state in Repositories, Label catalog, Templates, and Workflows shows a select-or-create-project CTA (not bare 'No project selected' text).
Label-catalog empty-list state renders an inline 'New definition' action.
Templates empty-list state renders an inline 'New Template' action.
SectionState's new `action`/`no-project` additions are additive and optional; existing call sites render unchanged (snapshot asserts this).
Tests assert the CTA renders in no-project and empty-list states.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` are green.
tasks.output: Extended SectionState.tsx; updated RepositoriesSection/LabelCatalogSection/TemplatesSection/WorkflowProfilesSection no-project + empty-list renderings + tests/snapshot.
tasks.notes: Per design D7. CTA target for 'no project' reuses the existing project switcher / CreateProject entry point (confirm exact entry from current shell code at implementation time). Broader cross-app EmptyState consolidation is out of scope.

tasks.title: Add Label catalog search input consistent with Templates
tasks.spec: specs/settings-content-consistency/spec.md#Label catalog provides a search input consistent with Templates
tasks.description: Add a search/filter input to LabelCatalogSection mirroring TemplatesSection's search behavior, with an accessible label (visible label or aria-label — NOT placeholder-only, which is itself an a11y gap). Filter the displayed label definitions by the query.
acceptanceCriteria: Label catalog renders a search/filter input when a project is selected.
Entering a query filters the displayed label definitions.
The search input exposes an accessible label (visible or aria-label), not placeholder-only.
Test asserts the input renders and that filtering changes the displayed list.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` are green.
tasks.notes: Per proposal/design consistency pass. TemplatesSection already has the search pattern to mirror.

tasks.title: Apply Settings typography baseline (text-balance / text-pretty / tabular-nums)
tasks.description:
Land the typography baseline from the single source of truth: in SettingsSection.tsx add `text-balance` to the

title and `text-pretty` to the

description (one edit uniformly affecting all sections, guaranteed by the settings-consistency contract test). Add `tabular-nums` to System InfoRow values and to Agent numeric/mono data rows. Do NOT put tabular-nums on the page title, and introduce NO new motion or gradients.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Settings section heading applies text-balance and every description applies text-pretty (via the SettingsSection SOT, not per-section).
System and Agent numeric/mono data rows apply tabular-nums; the page title does not.
No new animation or gradient effects are introduced.
The settings-consistency contract test (routing through SettingsSection/getSectionMeta + token rules) stays green.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` are green.
tasks.output: Updated SettingsSection.tsx (SOT heading/description classes), SystemSettingsSection.tsx + AgentSettingsSection.tsx (tabular-nums rows); contract test assertions.
tasks.notes: Per design D6. SOT edit avoids duplicating utilities 9x and risking contract-test drift.
